segments.t: In his dressing room after an emotional day of filming, Hervé chats with makeup artist Vero. Impressed by his natural acting talent, Vero shares an exciting rumor she overheard from the film director. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Hervé, je suis très occupée aujourd'hui.
Tout est prêt dans ta loge.
Bien sûr Véro, pas de souci.
Tu étais encore extraordinaire sur le plateau!
Merci, c'était vraiment très intense.
Mais le tournage passe tellement vite.
Je veux encore profiter de ça.
Écoute, j'ai un grand secret.
Ta carrière d'acteur continue peut-être!
Quoi? Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
Valérie pense à toi maintenant.
Elle prépare son prochain grand film.
Elle veut te donner un vrai rôle!
C'est le plus beau jour!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Hervé, je suis très occupée aujourd'hui.
'Hervé, I am very busy today.' Vero pops into the room while juggling several tasks on set. The feminine adjective 'occupee' means busy.
Tout est prêt dans ta loge.
'Everything is ready in your dressing room.' She lets him know that the makeup remover is laid out. In theater and film, 'loge' designates a performer's dressing room.
Bien sûr Véro, pas de souci.
'Of course Vero, no problem.' Hervé is happy to remove his own makeup without fuss. The casual phrase 'pas de souci' means no worries or no problem.
Tu étais encore extraordinaire sur le plateau!
'You were amazing again on the set!' Vero compliments his moving performance in front of the crew. The noun 'plateau' refers to a film set.
Merci, c'était vraiment très intense.
'Thank you, it was truly very intense.' Hervé is still emotional from acting out the dramatic scene. The adjective 'intense' is identical in French and English.
Mais le tournage passe tellement vite.
'But the shoot goes by so fast.' Hervé wishes his time as an actor did not end so quickly. The masculine noun 'tournage' means film shoot.
Je veux encore profiter de ça.
'I still want to enjoy this.' He wants to savor every moment on set before returning to agency desk work. The verb 'profiter de' means to enjoy or make the most of.
Écoute, j'ai un grand secret.
'Listen, I have a big secret.' Vero lowers her voice to share confidential gossip from the crew. The imperative 'ecoute' calls for close attention.
Ta carrière d'acteur continue peut-être!
'Your acting career continues perhaps!' Vero hints that this small part might lead to more roles. The adverb 'peut-etre' means maybe or perhaps.
Quoi? Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
'What? What are you saying?' Hervé widens his eyes in disbelief and excitement. The verb 'dis' comes from 'dire', meaning to say.
Valérie pense à toi maintenant.
'Valerie is thinking of you now.' Vero reveals that the film director was praising Hervé earlier. The construction 'penser a' takes a stressed pronoun like 'toi'.
Elle prépare son prochain grand film.
'She is preparing her next big film.' The director is already planning her upcoming feature project. The adjective 'prochain' means next.
Elle veut te donner un vrai rôle!
'She wants to give you a real role!' Vero adds that the director has a major part in mind for him. The adjective 'vrai' placed before a noun means real or genuine.
C'est le plus beau jour!

'It is the most beautiful day!' Hervé beams with joy at the prospect of becoming a real movie star. The superlative 'le plus beau' means the most beautiful or best. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Mais le tournage passe tellement vite.

Ta carrière d'acteur continue peut-être!

Valérie pense à toi maintenant.
Elle prépare son prochain grand film.

C'est le plus beau jour!

Thrilled by Vero's secret news, Hervé gazes into the dressing room mirror like a true cinema star. His brief adventure on a movie set may be the beginning of an unexpected new calling. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
Bravo, ma nouvelle grande étoile!
